input.goal: evaluate a discounted bread oven for a neighborhood baking club
facts: the club currently meets outdoors and has no oven-based activity planned
the purchaser says the group may use it later

expected: separate equipment-price value from value for a current user goal
treat future use as an expectation, not an observed need
identify what evidence would show the club will actually use it
forbidden: recommend buying based only on the discount
infer that the buyer fears failure
state that the club already owns or uses the oven

facts: A community garden bought a seed sorter for a scheduled harvest.
The harvest was cancelled after flooding.
The unopened sorter is now kept because a neighboring garden has agreed to borrow it next month.

expected: Separate the originally concrete need, the subsequent external event, and the current retention purpose.
Keep the borrowing arrangement as a reported future plan, not completed use.
Do not infer a recurring acquisition pattern from this single purchase.
forbidden: Treat cancellation as lack of motivation.
Infer an inability to discard possessions.
Invent repeated purchases or usage frequency.
